status: Desk estimate. Polkadot's published metanode spec priced against Hetzner list prices. No operator has tested it. Hardware and bandwidth only: no labour, no RPC or light-client load figures.
duty: Validate, collate Asset Hub and People, serve relay chain, Asset Hub and People RPC and smoldot light clients over WebRTC

validator.cpu: 8 physical cores at 3.4 GHz, SMT off

collator_each.storage: 200+ GB NVMe, pruned, relay data read from the validator via --relay-chain-rpc-urls

prices.source: hetzner.com list prices, Falkenstein, excluding VAT, read 2026-11-27

AX102.hardware: Ryzen 9 7950X3D 16 cores, 128 GB DDR5 ECC, 2 x 1.92 TB NVMe, 1 Gbit/s

AX42.hardware: Ryzen 7 PRO 8700GE 8 cores, 64 GB DDR5 ECC, 2 x 512 GB NVMe, 1 Gbit/s

options.name: Same duty, both collators on one separate box
Same duty, one box per service as the page splits it
All five Kusama system chains
options.machines: AX102 + 3 AX42, two collators a box at most

assumptions: Option 1 meets the minimum single-machine spec, not the optimal 24 cores. 2.4 TB means striping the two drives with no mirror, or larger drives at a price not read.
Option 2 puts two collators on one 8-core, 64 GB box, which fits the minimum exactly and leaves nothing spare.
Option 4 gives Bridge Hub, Coretime and Encointer the Asset Hub spec. The page prices none of them, and Bridge Hub's relaying may need more.
Every seat is costed as if it collates. Kusama had 54 collator slots on 2026-11-04, 25 on Asset Hub and People (collator-slots-2026-11-04.json), so the collator part is an upper bound.
96 seats is the shape in Kusama referendum 573. 300 is where Ref 681 stops.
The minimum spec is assumed to survive real RPC and light-client load. Nobody has shown that.
